translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, ploughing was performed personally.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was complete, ploughing was performed personally.

sentences.zh: 先祠，司農進穜懸之種，六宮主之。

translations.literal: Before sacrifice, the Director of Agriculture presented the selected seed; the Six Palaces presided.
translations.idiomatic: Before sacrifice, the Director of Agriculture presented the selected seed; the Six Palaces presided.

sentences.zh: 行事之官並齋，設齋省。

translations.literal: Officials performing the rite all fasted; a fasting quarter was established.
translations.idiomatic: Officials performing the rite all fasted; a fasting quarter was established.

sentences.zh: 于壇所列宮懸。

translations.literal: Palace bells were arranged at the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Palace bells were arranged at the altar.

sentences.zh: 又置先農坐於壇上。

translations.literal: The First Farmer seat was also placed on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The First Farmer seat was also placed on the altar.

sentences.zh: 眾官朝服，司空一獻，不燎。

translations.literal: All officials in court dress; the Director of Works one presentation, no fire offering.
translations.idiomatic: All officials in court dress; the Director of Works one presentation, no fire offering.

sentences.zh: 祠訖，皇帝乃服通天冠、青紗袍、黑介幘，佩蒼玉，黃綬，青帶、襪、舄，備法駕，乘木輅。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, the emperor then wore the Tongtian crown, blue gauze robe, black headcloth, azure jade pendant with yellow sash, blue belt, socks, and shoes, with full imperial regalia, riding the wood chariot.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was complete, the emperor then wore the Tongtian crown, blue gauze robe, black headcloth, azure jade pendant with yellow sash, blue belt, socks, and shoes, with full imperial regalia, riding the wood chariot.

sentences.zh: 耕官具朝服從。

translations.literal: Ploughing officials all in court dress followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ploughing officials all in court dress followed.

sentences.zh: 殿中監進禦耒于壇南，百官定列。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace presented the imperial plough south of the altar; all officials took their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace presented the imperial plough south of the altar; all officials took their places.

sentences.zh: 帝出便殿，升耕，壇南陛，即御座。

translations.literal: The emperor came out of the side hall, ascended the ploughing altar's southern stairway, and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came out of the side hall, ascended the ploughing altar's southern stairway, and took the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 應耕者各進於列。

translations.literal: Those who should plough each advanced to their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those who should plough each advanced to their rank.

sentences.zh: 帝降自南陛，至耕位，釋劍執耒，三推三反，升壇即坐。

translations.literal: The emperor descended the southern stairway to the ploughing position, set aside his sword and took the plough, three pushes and three returns, ascended the altar and sat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended the southern stairway to the ploughing position, set aside his sword and took the plough, three pushes and three returns, ascended the altar and sat.

sentences.zh: 耕官一品五推五反，二品七推七反，三品九推九反。

translations.literal: First-rank ploughing officials five pushes and five returns, second rank seven pushes and seven returns, third rank nine pushes and nine returns.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank ploughing officials five pushes and five returns, second rank seven pushes and seven returns, third rank nine pushes and nine returns.

sentences.zh: 藉田令帥其屬以牛耕，終千畝。

translations.literal: The sacred field director led his subordinates to plough with oxen, completing a thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred field director led his subordinates to plough with oxen, completing a thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 以青箱奉穜「Ｌ種，跪呈司農，詣耕所灑之。

translations.literal: With a green box carrying selected seed, kneeling to present to the Director of Agriculture, proceeding to the ploughing site to scatter it.
translations.idiomatic: With a green box carrying selected seed, kneeling to present to the Director of Agriculture, proceeding to the ploughing site to scatter it.

sentences.zh: 櫌訖，司農省功，奏事畢。

translations.literal: When pounding was complete, the Director of Agriculture inspected the work and memorialized; the affair was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When pounding was complete, the Director of Agriculture inspected the work and memorialized; the affair was complete.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降之便殿，更衣饗宴。

translations.literal: The emperor descended to the side hall, changed clothes, and feasted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended to the side hall, changed clothes, and feasted.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，班賚而還。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, rewards were distributed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, rewards were distributed and he returned.

sentences.zh: 隋制，于國南十四裏啟夏門外，置地千畝，為壇，孟春吉亥，祭先農於其上，以後稷配。

translations.literal: Sui practice: fourteen li south of the capital outside the Qixia Gate, a thousand mu of land was set aside and an altar made; on a fortunate hai day in the first month of spring, the First Farmer was sacrificed to upon it, with Hou Ji associated.
translations.idiomatic: Sui practice: fourteen li south of the capital outside the Qixia Gate, a thousand mu of land was set aside and an altar made; on a fortunate hai day in the first month of spring, the First Farmer was sacrificed to upon it, with Hou Ji associated.

sentences.zh: 牲用一太牢。

translations.literal: Victims were one great offering.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were one great offering.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，備法駕，乘金根車。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the dragon-and-phoenix crown robe, with full imperial regalia, riding the gold-root chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the dragon-and-phoenix crown robe, with full imperial regalia, riding the gold-root chariot.

sentences.zh: 禮三獻訖，因耕。

translations.literal: When the triple presentation was complete, ploughing followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the triple presentation was complete, ploughing followed.

sentences.zh: 司農授耒，皇帝三推訖，執事者以授應耕者，各以班五推九推。

translations.literal: The Director of Agriculture presented the plough; when the emperor's three pushes were complete, active officials received it and each according to rank performed five or nine pushes.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Agriculture presented the plough; when the emperor's three pushes were complete, active officials received it and each according to rank performed five or nine pushes.

sentences.zh: 而司徒帥其屬終千畝。

translations.literal: The Grand Steward then led his subordinates to complete a thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward then led his subordinates to complete a thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 播殖九谷，納於神倉，以擬粢盛。

translations.literal: Nine grains were sown, stored in the spirit granary to supply grain offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Nine grains were sown, stored in the spirit granary to supply grain offerings.

sentences.zh: 穰稿以餉犧牲雲。

translations.literal: Stalks and chaff were used to feed sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: Stalks and chaff were used to feed sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》王后蠶于北郊，而漢法皇后蠶于東郊。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: the queen raised silkworms at the northern suburb; Han practice: the empress raised silkworms at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou: the queen raised silkworms at the northern suburb; Han practice: the empress raised silkworms at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 魏遵《周禮》，蠶於北郊。

translations.literal: Wei followed the Rites of Zhou, raising silkworms at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Wei followed the Rites of Zhou, raising silkworms at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 吳韋昭制《西蠶頌》，則孫氏亦有其禮矣。

translations.literal: Wu's Wei Zhao composed the 'Western Silkworm Eulogy'—then the Sun house also had this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's Wei Zhao composed the 'Western Silkworm Eulogy'—then the Sun house also had this rite.

sentences.zh: 晉太康六年，武帝楊皇后蠶于西郊，依漢故事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taikang under Jin, Emperor Wu's Empress Yang raised silkworms at the western suburb, following Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taikang under Jin, Emperor Wu's Empress Yang raised silkworms at the western suburb, following Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 江左至宋孝武大明四年，始於台城西白石裏為西蠶，設兆域。

translations.literal: The Jiang-zuo down to Emperor Xiaowu of Song in the fourth year of Daming first established the western silkworm at Baishi west of Taicheng, setting up a precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-zuo down to Emperor Xiaowu of Song in the fourth year of Daming first established the western silkworm at Baishi west of Taicheng, setting up a precinct.

sentences.zh: 置大殿七間，又立蠶觀。

translations.literal: A great hall of seven bays was built; a Silkworm Pavilion was also established.
translations.idiomatic: A great hall of seven bays was built; a Silkworm Pavilion was also established.

sentences.zh: 自是有其禮。

translations.literal: From this time the rite existed.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the rite existed.

sentences.zh: 後齊為蠶坊於京城北之西，去皇宮十八裏之外，方千步。

translations.literal: Later Qi made a silkworm compound northwest of the capital, eighteen li outside the palace, a thousand paces square.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi made a silkworm compound northwest of the capital, eighteen li outside the palace, a thousand paces square.

sentences.zh: 蠶宮，方九十步，牆高一丈五尺，被以棘。

translations.literal: The Silkworm Palace was ninety paces square, walls one zhang five chi high, covered with thorns.
translations.idiomatic: The Silkworm Palace was ninety paces square, walls one zhang five chi high, covered with thorns.

sentences.zh: 其中起蠶室二十七口，別殿一區。

translations.literal: Within it twenty-seven silkworm chambers were built, and one separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: Within it twenty-seven silkworm chambers were built, and one separate hall.

sentences.zh: 置蠶宮，令丞佐史，皆宦者為之。

translations.literal: Silkworm Palace director, assistant, and clerks were all eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworm Palace director, assistant, and clerks were all eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 路西置皇后蠶壇，高四尺，方二丈，四出，階廣八尺。

translations.literal: West of the road the empress's silkworm altar was placed, four chi high and two zhang square, projecting on four sides, stairways eight chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: West of the road the empress's silkworm altar was placed, four chi high and two zhang square, projecting on four sides, stairways eight chi wide.

sentences.zh: 置先蠶壇于桑壇東南，大路東，橫路之南。

translations.literal: The First Silkworm altar was placed southeast of the mulberry altar, east of the great road, south of the cross-road.
translations.idiomatic: The First Silkworm altar was placed southeast of the mulberry altar, east of the great road, south of the cross-road.

sentences.zh: 壇高五尺，方二丈，四出，階廣五尺。

translations.literal: The altar was five chi high and two zhang square, projecting on four sides, stairways five chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: The altar was five chi high and two zhang square, projecting on four sides, stairways five chi wide.

sentences.zh: 外兆方四十步，面開一門。

translations.literal: The outer precinct was forty paces square, with one gate opening on the face.
translations.idiomatic: The outer precinct was forty paces square, with one gate opening on the face.

sentences.zh: 有綠衤詹襦、褠衣、黃履，以供蠶母。

translations.literal: There were green padded jackets, work clothes, and yellow shoes to supply the silkworm mothers.
translations.idiomatic: There were green padded jackets, work clothes, and yellow shoes to supply the silkworm mothers.

sentences.zh: 每歲季春，穀雨後吉日，使公卿以一太牢祀先蠶黃帝軒轅氏於壇上，無配，如祀先農。

translations.literal: Each year in the last month of spring, on a fortunate day after Grain Rain, dukes and ministers were sent to sacrifice with one great offering to the First Silkworm Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan on the altar, without association, as in sacrificing to the First Farmer.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the last month of spring, on a fortunate day after Grain Rain, dukes and ministers were sent to sacrifice with one great offering to the First Silkworm Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan on the altar, without association, as in sacrificing to the First Farmer.

sentences.zh: 禮訖，皇后因親桑于桑壇。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the empress personally picked mulberry leaves at the mulberry altar.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the empress personally picked mulberry leaves at the mulberry altar.

sentences.zh: 備法駕，服鞠衣，乘重翟，帥六宮升桑壇東陛，即御座。

translations.literal: With full imperial regalia, wearing the ju robe, riding the heavy pheasant chariot, leading the Six Palaces up the mulberry altar's eastern stairway to the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: With full imperial regalia, wearing the ju robe, riding the heavy pheasant chariot, leading the Six Palaces up the mulberry altar's eastern stairway to the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 女尚書執筐，女主衣執鉤，立壇下。

translations.literal: The Female Master of Writing held the basket; the Mistress of Female Attire held the hook, standing below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The Female Master of Writing held the basket; the Mistress of Female Attire held the hook, standing below the altar.

sentences.zh: 皇后降自東陛，執筐者處右，執鉤者居左，蠶母在後。

translations.literal: The empress descended the eastern stairway; the basket-holder was on the right, the hook-holder on the left, silkworm mothers behind.
translations.idiomatic: The empress descended the eastern stairway; the basket-holder was on the right, the hook-holder on the left, silkworm mothers behind.

sentences.zh: 乃躬桑三條訖，升壇，即御座。

translations.literal: She personally picked three branches, ascended the altar, and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: She personally picked three branches, ascended the altar, and took the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 內命婦以次就桑，鞠衣五條，展衣七條，褖衣九條，以授蠶母。

translations.literal: Inner appointed women in turn picked mulberry—five branches in ju robes, seven in zhan robes, nine in tuan robes—to give to the silkworm mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Inner appointed women in turn picked mulberry—five branches in ju robes, seven in zhan robes, nine in tuan robes—to give to the silkworm mothers.

sentences.zh: 還蠶室，切之授世婦，灑一簿。

translations.literal: Returning to the Silkworm Palace, cutting and giving to the palace women, scattering one sheet.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the Silkworm Palace, cutting and giving to the palace women, scattering one sheet.

sentences.zh: 預桑者並複本位。

translations.literal: Those who had picked mulberry all returned to their original places.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had picked mulberry all returned to their original places.

sentences.zh: 後乃降壇，還便殿，改服，設勞酒，班賚而還。

translations.literal: Then descending the altar, returning to the side hall, changing clothes, setting out refreshment wine, distributing rewards and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Then descending the altar, returning to the side hall, changing clothes, setting out refreshment wine, distributing rewards and returning.

sentences.zh: 後周制，皇后乘翠輅，率三妃、三昿弋、禦媛、禦婉、三公夫人、三孤內子至蠶所，以一太牢親祭，進奠先蠶西陵氏神。

translations.literal: Later Zhou practice: the empress rode the kingfisher chariot, leading three consorts, three yi, yu, imperial attendants, and ladies, the Three Excellencies' wives, and the Three Solitaries' inner ladies to the silkworm site, personally sacrificing with one great offering, presenting to the First Silkworm Spirit of Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou practice: the empress rode the kingfisher chariot, leading three consorts, three yi, yu, imperial attendants, and ladies, the Three Excellencies' wives, and the Three Solitaries' inner ladies to the silkworm site, personally sacrificing with one great offering, presenting to the First Silkworm Spirit of Xiling.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，降壇，昭化嬪亞獻，淑嬪終獻，因以公桑焉。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, descending the altar, the Zhaohua Lady made the secondary presentation, the Shubi Lady the final presentation, then proceeding to the public mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, descending the altar, the Zhaohua Lady made the secondary presentation, the Shubi Lady the final presentation, then proceeding to the public mulberry.

sentences.zh: 隋制，于宮北三裏為壇，高四尺。

translations.literal: Sui practice: three li north of the palace an altar was made, four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Sui practice: three li north of the palace an altar was made, four chi high.

sentences.zh: 季春上巳，皇后服鞠衣，乘重翟，率三夫人、九嬪、內外命婦，以一太牢，制幣，祭先蠶於壇上，用一獻禮。

translations.literal: On shangsi day in the last month of spring, the empress wore the ju robe, rode the heavy pheasant chariot, leading three ladies, nine concubines, and inner and outer appointed women, with one great offering and presentation silks, sacrificing to the First Silkworm on the altar, using one presentation.
translations.idiomatic: On shangsi day in the last month of spring, the empress wore the ju robe, rode the heavy pheasant chariot, leading three ladies, nine concubines, and inner and outer appointed women, with one great offering and presentation silks, sacrificing to the First Silkworm on the altar, using one presentation.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，就桑位於壇南，東面。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, she took the mulberry-picking position south of the altar, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was complete, she took the mulberry-picking position south of the altar, facing east.

sentences.zh: 尚功進金鉤，典制奉筐。

translations.literal: The Chief of Works presented the gold hook; the Director of Regulations presented the basket.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief of Works presented the gold hook; the Director of Regulations presented the basket.

sentences.zh: 皇后采三條，反鉤。

translations.literal: The empress picked three branches and returned the hook.
translations.idiomatic: The empress picked three branches and returned the hook.

sentences.zh: 命婦各依班采，五條九條而止。

translations.literal: Appointed women each picked according to rank, stopping at five or nine branches.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed women each picked according to rank, stopping at five or nine branches.

sentences.zh: 世婦亦有蠶母受切桑，灑訖，還依位。

translations.literal: Palace women also had silkworm mothers receive cut mulberry; when scattering was complete, all returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women also had silkworm mothers receive cut mulberry; when scattering was complete, all returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 皇后乃還宮。

translations.literal: The empress then returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 自後齊、後周及隋，其典大抵多依晉儀。

translations.literal: From Later Qi, Later Zhou, and Sui, the canon largely followed Jin practice.
translations.idiomatic: From Later Qi, Later Zhou, and Sui, the canon largely followed Jin practice.

sentences.zh: 然亦時有損益矣。

translations.literal: Yet there were also additions and subtractions from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there were also additions and subtractions from time to time.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：仲春以玄鳥至之日，用太牢祀于高禖。

translations.literal: The Rites: in the second month on the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice with the great offering at the High Altar of Procreation.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites prescribe that in the second month on the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice with the great offering at the High Altar of Procreation.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝年二十九，乃得太子，甚喜，為立禖祠于城南，祀以特牲，因有其祀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han at age twenty-nine finally obtained the heir—greatly rejoicing, he established a procreation shrine south of the city, sacrificing with a single victim; thus the sacrifice existed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han at age twenty-nine finally obtained the heir—greatly rejoicing, he established a procreation shrine south of the city, sacrificing with a single victim; thus the sacrifice existed.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康六年，禖壇石中破為二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the procreation altar stone broke in two in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the procreation altar stone broke in two in the middle.

sentences.zh: 詔問石毀今應複不，博士議：「《禮》無高禖置石之文，未知造設所由；

translations.literal: An edict asked whether the stone's destruction should now be restored; erudites submitted an opinion: 'The Rites have no text on placing a stone at the High Altar of Procreation—the origin of its establishment is unknown;'
translations.idiomatic: The court asked whether the broken stone should be restored. The erudites replied that the Rites contain no provision for a stone at the High Altar of Procreation, and the reason for its original placement is unknown.

sentences.zh: 既已毀破，可無改造。

translations.literal: since it is already destroyed, it need not be rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Since it was already broken, they argued, it need not be replaced.

sentences.zh: 」更下西府博議。

translations.literal: It was referred down to the Western Secretariat for broader discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The question was referred to the Western Secretariat for further deliberation.

sentences.zh: 而賊曹屬束皙議：「以石在壇上，蓋主道也。

translations.literal: Shu Xi of the Bandit Bureau submitted an opinion: 'Since the stone is on the altar, it probably governs the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi of the Bandit Bureau countered that a stone on the altar likely embodied the ritual Way itself.

sentences.zh: 祭器弊則埋而置新，今宜埋而更造，不宜遂廢。

translations.literal: When sacrificial vessels are worn out they are buried and new ones set out—now it is appropriate to bury and rebuild, not to abolish outright.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrificial vessels wear out, the old are buried and new ones installed; the broken stone should be treated the same—buried and replaced, not simply abandoned.

sentences.zh: 」時此議不用。

translations.literal: At that time this opinion was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, this opinion was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 後得高堂隆故事，魏青龍中，造立此石，詔更鐫石，令如舊，置高禖壇上。

translations.literal: Later the precedent of Gao Tanglong was obtained—in the Qinglong period of Wei this stone was made and erected; an edict ordered the stone recarved like the old and placed on the High Altar of Procreation.
translations.idiomatic: Later the precedent of Gao Tanglong came to light: in Wei's Qinglong era such a stone had been made and erected, and an edict ordered a new stone carved to match the old and placed on the High Altar of Procreation.

sentences.zh: 埋破石入地一丈。

translations.literal: The broken stone was buried one zhang into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The broken stone was buried one zhang deep in the earth.

sentences.zh: 案梁太廟北門內道西有石，文如竹葉，小屋覆之，宋元嘉中修廟所得。

translations.literal: Examining the Liang Grand Temple, west of the road inside the north gate there was a stone with writing like bamboo leaves, covered by a small house—obtained when the temple was repaired in the Yuanjia period.
translations.idiomatic: At the Liang Grand Temple, west of the road inside the north gate, stood a stone inscribed with bamboo-leaf script, sheltered by a small pavilion—it had been found when the temple was repaired in the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 陸澄以為孝武時郊禖之石。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng held it to be the stone of the suburban procreation sacrifice under Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng identified it as the stone from Emperor Xiaowu's suburban procreation sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 然則江左亦有此禮矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Jiang-zuo also had this rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Jiang-zuo court also observed this rite.

sentences.zh: 後齊高禖，為壇於南郊傍，廣輪二十六尺，高九尺，四陛三壝。

translations.literal: Later Qi's High Altar of Procreation: an altar was made beside the southern suburb, twenty-six chi in circumference and nine chi high, with four stairways and three enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi's High Altar of Procreation stood beside the southern suburb—twenty-six chi around, nine chi high, with four stairways and three enclosures.

sentences.zh: 每歲春分玄鳥至之日，皇帝親帥六宮，祀青帝於壇，乙太昊配，而祀高禖之神以祈子。

translations.literal: Each year on the day the dark bird arrives at the spring equinox, the emperor personally led the Six Palaces to sacrifice to the Green Emperor at the altar, with Taihao associated, and to sacrifice to the High Altar of Procreation spirit to pray for children.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on the spring-equinox day when the dark bird arrived, the emperor personally led the Six Palaces to sacrifice to the Green Emperor at the altar—with Taihao as associated offering—and to pray for heirs at the High Altar of Procreation.

sentences.zh: 其儀，青帝北方南向，配帝東方西向，禖神壇下東陛之南，西向。

translations.literal: The ceremony: the Green Emperor north facing south, the associated emperor east facing west; the Procreation spirit below the altar at the south of the eastern stairway, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In the ceremony the Green Emperor stood in the north facing south, the associated emperor in the east facing west, and the Procreation spirit below the altar at the south side of the eastern stairway, facing west.

sentences.zh: 禮用青珪束帛，牲共以一太牢。

translations.literal: The rite used green jade tablet and bundled silks; victims together one great offering.
translations.idiomatic: The rite employed a green jade tablet and bundled silks, with a single great offering as victim.

sentences.zh: 祀日，皇帝服袞冕，乘玉輅。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day the emperor wore the dragon-and-phoenix crown robe and rode the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day the emperor wore the dragon-and-phoenix crown robe and rode the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 皇后服褘衣，乘重翟。

translations.literal: The empress wore the hui robe and rode the heavy pheasant chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore the hui robe and rode the heavy pheasant chariot.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，降自東陛，皇后亞獻，降自西陛，並詣便坐。

translations.literal: The emperor's initial presentation—descending the eastern stairway; the empress's secondary presentation—descending the western stairway; both proceeding to the side seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made the initial presentation, descending the eastern stairway; the empress made the secondary presentation, descending the western stairway; both then proceeded to the side seat.

sentences.zh: 夫人終獻，上嬪獻於禖神訖。

translations.literal: The Lady's final presentation; the Senior Lady presented at the Procreation spirit and finished.
translations.idiomatic: A lady made the final presentation; a senior lady presented at the Procreation spirit to complete the rite.

sentences.zh: 帝及後並詣欑位，乃送神。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress both proceeded to the spirit seat, then sent off the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress both proceeded to the spirit seat before sending the spirit away.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皇后及群官皆拜。

translations.literal: The emperor, empress, and all officials all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, empress, and all officials bowed together.

sentences.zh: 乃撤就燎，禮畢而還。

translations.literal: Then withdrew to fire offering; when the rite was complete they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings were then committed to the fire; when the rite was complete they returned.

sentences.zh: 隋制亦以玄鳥至之日，祀高禖於南郊壇。

translations.literal: Sui practice also on the day the dark bird arrives sacrificed at the High Altar of Procreation at the southern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui practice as well, on the day the dark bird arrived sacrifice was performed at the High Altar of Procreation within the southern suburban precinct.

sentences.zh: 牲用太牢一。

translations.literal: Victims were one great offering.
translations.idiomatic: The victim was a single great offering.

sentences.zh: 舊禮祀司中、司命、風師、雨師之法，皆隨其類而祭之。

translations.literal: The old rite for sacrificing to the Director of Fate, Director of Life, Wind Lord, and Rain Master—all sacrificed according to their category.
translations.idiomatic: The old rites for the Director of Fate, Director of Life, Wind Lord, and Rain Master all classified each spirit and sacrificed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 兆風師於西方者，就秋風之勁，而不從箕星之位。

translations.literal: The Wind Lord's precinct in the west—approaching the strength of autumn wind, not following the position of the Winnowing-Basket star.
translations.idiomatic: The Wind Lord's precinct was placed in the west to align with the force of autumn wind, rather than with the Winnowing-Basket constellation.

sentences.zh: 兆司中、司命於南郊，以天神是陽，故兆於南郊也。

translations.literal: The Director of Fate and Director of Life at the southern suburb—because heavenly spirits are yang, therefore the precinct is at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Fate and Director of Life were placed at the southern suburb because heavenly spirits belong to yang, and the southern suburb is the yang precinct.

sentences.zh: 兆雨師於北郊者，就水位，在北也。

translations.literal: The Rain Master's precinct at the northern suburb—approaching the water position, in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Rain Master's precinct stood at the northern suburb, aligned with the water element in the north.

sentences.zh: 隋制，于國城西北十裏亥地，為司中、司命、司祿三壇，同壝。

translations.literal: Sui practice: ten li northwest of the capital in the hai position, three altars for the Director of Fate, Director of Life, and Director of Salary, sharing one enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui practice, ten li northwest of the capital in the hai position, three altars for the Director of Fate, Director of Life, and Director of Salary shared a single enclosure.

sentences.zh: 祀以立冬後亥。

translations.literal: Sacrifice after hai day following the Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice was performed on the hai day following the Start of Winter.

sentences.zh: 國城東北七裏通化門外為風師壇，祀以立春後醜。

translations.literal: Seven li northeast of the capital outside the Tonghua Gate was the Wind Lord altar; sacrifice after chou day following the Establishment of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Seven li northeast of the capital outside the Tonghua Gate stood the Wind Lord altar, where sacrifice followed the chou day after the Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 國城西南八裏金光門外為雨師壇，祀以立夏後申。

translations.literal: Eight li southwest of the capital outside the Jinguang Gate was the Rain Master altar; sacrifice after shen day following the Establishment of Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Eight li southwest of the capital outside the Jinguang Gate stood the Rain Master altar, where sacrifice followed the shen day after the Establishment of Summer.

sentences.zh: 壇皆三尺，牲以一少牢。

translations.literal: Altars were all three chi high; victims one secondary offering.
translations.idiomatic: All altars were three chi high; victims consisted of a single secondary offering.

sentences.zh: 昔伊耆氏始為蠟。

translations.literal: In antiquity Emperor Yi first performed the la sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Emperor Yi first instituted the la sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蠟者，索也。

translations.literal: La means 'to seek.'
translations.idiomatic: La means 'to seek out.'

sentences.zh: 古之君子，使人必報之。

translations.literal: The gentlemen of antiquity, when sending people out, required them to report back.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of antiquity required those they sent forth to return and report.

sentences.zh: 故周法，以歲十二月，合聚萬物而索饗之。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou practice, in the twelfth month of the year, gathered all things together and sought to feast them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in Zhou practice, in the twelfth month, all things were gathered together and offered a feast of thanks.

sentences.zh: 仁之至，義之盡也。

translations.literal: Benevolence at its utmost, righteousness at its fullest.
translations.idiomatic: This was benevolence at its utmost and righteousness at its fullest.

sentences.zh: 其祭法，四方各自祭之。

translations.literal: The sacrificial law: each direction sacrificed separately.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial law required each direction to be honored separately.

sentences.zh: 若不成之方，則闕而不祭。

translations.literal: If a direction's harvest was not complete, that direction's sacrifice was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: If a direction's harvest failed, that direction's sacrifice was omitted.

sentences.zh: 後周亦存其典，常以十一月，祭神農氏、伊耆氏、後稷氏、田畯、鱗、羽、臝、毛、介、水、墉、坊、郵、表、畷、獸、貓之神於五郊。

translations.literal: Later Zhou also preserved this canon, regularly in the eleventh month sacrificing to the spirits of Shennong, Emperor Yi, Hou Ji, the Field Director, scales, feathers, naked creatures, fur, shell, water, walls, dikes, post stations, boundary markers, field paths, beasts, and cats at the five suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou also preserved this canon, regularly in the eleventh month sacrificing at the five suburbs to the spirits of Shennong, Emperor Yi, Hou Ji, the Field Director, and all creatures and features of the land—from scales and feathers to walls, dikes, post stations, boundary markers, field paths, beasts, and cats.

sentences.zh: 五方上帝、地祇、五星、列宿、蒼龍、硃雀、白獸、玄武、五人帝、五官之神、嶽鎮海瀆、山林川澤、丘陵墳衍原隰，各分其方，合祭之。

translations.literal: The Five Directional Heavenly Emperors, earth spirits, Five Stars, stellar lodges, azure dragon, vermilion bird, white beast, black warrior, Five Human Emperors, Five Officials, sacred peaks, seas, rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands—each divided by direction, combined in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Directional Heavenly Emperors, earth spirits, Five Stars, stellar lodges, azure dragon, vermilion bird, white beast, black warrior, Five Human Emperors, Five Officials, and all sacred peaks, seas, rivers, mountains, forests, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands were each assigned to a direction and honored in combined sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 日月，五方皆祭之。

translations.literal: Sun and moon—sacrificed in all five directions.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon received sacrifice in all five directions.

sentences.zh: 上帝、地祇、神農、伊耆、人帝於壇上，南郊則以神農，既蠟，無其祀。

translations.literal: Heavenly Emperor, earth spirit, Shennong, Emperor Yi, and Human Emperors on the altar; at the southern suburb Shennong—after la, no separate sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Emperor, earth spirit, Shennong, Emperor Yi, and Human Emperors stood on the altar; at the southern suburb Shennong was honored—after the la rite, no separate sacrifice was needed.

sentences.zh: 三辰七宿則為小壇於其側，嶽鎮海瀆、山林川澤、丘陵墳衍原隰，則各為坎，余則於平地。

translations.literal: The Three Stars and Seven Lodges were made into small altars at their sides; sacred peaks, seas, rivers, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands each made into pits; the remainder on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Stars and Seven Lodges received small side altars; sacred peaks, seas, rivers, mountains, forests, marshes, hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands each received pits; the remainder were honored on level ground.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻上帝、地祗、神農、伊耆及人帝，塚宰亞獻，宗伯終獻。

translations.literal: The emperor's initial presentation to the Heavenly Emperor, earth spirit, Shennong, Emperor Yi, and Human Emperors; the Grand Steward secondary presentation, the Grand Herald final presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made the initial presentation to the Heavenly Emperor, earth spirit, Shennong, Emperor Yi, and Human Emperors; the Grand Steward made the secondary presentation and the Grand Herald the final presentation.

sentences.zh: 上大夫獻三辰、五官、後稷、田畯、嶽鎮海瀆，中大夫獻七宿、山林川澤已下。

translations.literal: Senior grand masters presented the Three Stars, Five Officials, Hou Ji, Field Director, and sacred peaks, seas, and rivers; middle grand masters presented the Seven Lodges, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, and below.
translations.idiomatic: Senior grand masters presented offerings to the Three Stars, Five Officials, Hou Ji, Field Director, and sacred peaks, seas, and rivers; middle grand masters presented to the Seven Lodges, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, and below.

sentences.zh: 自天帝、人帝、田畯、羽毛之類，牲幣玉帛皆從燎；

translations.literal: From the Heavenly Emperor, Human Emperors, Field Director, feathers, and the like—victims, silks, jades, and silks all followed fire offering;
translations.idiomatic: For the Heavenly Emperor, Human Emperors, Field Director, feathered creatures, and the like, victims, silks, and jades were all committed to fire;

sentences.zh: 地祇、郵、表、畷之類，皆從埋。

translations.literal: earth spirits, post stations, boundary markers, field paths, and the like—all followed burial.
translations.idiomatic: for earth spirits, post stations, boundary markers, field paths, and the like, all offerings were buried.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，皇帝如南郊便殿致齋，明日乃蠟祭於南郊，如東郊儀。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, the emperor proceeded to the southern suburb side hall for fasting; the next day la sacrifice at the southern suburb, as at the eastern suburb ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice was complete, the emperor retired to the southern suburb side hall to fast; the next day the la sacrifice was performed at the southern suburb, following the eastern suburban ceremony.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，又如黃郊便殿致齋，明日乃祭。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, again fasting at the yellow suburb side hall; the next day sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When that rite was complete, he again fasted at the yellow suburb side hall and sacrificed the next day.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，又如西郊便殿，明日乃祭。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, again at the western suburb side hall; the next day sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When that rite was complete, he again retired to the western suburb side hall and sacrificed the next day.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，又如北郊便殿，明日蠟祭訖，還宮。

translations.literal: When sacrifice was complete, again at the northern suburb side hall; the next day when la sacrifice was complete, returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When that rite was complete, he again retired to the northern suburb side hall; the next day, when the la sacrifice was complete, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 隋初因周制，定令亦以孟冬下亥蠟百神，臘宗廟，祭社稷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui, following Zhou practice, regulations also fixed la in the last ten days of the first month of winter to feast the hundred spirits, la at the ancestral temple, and sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui, following Zhou practice, regulations fixed the la feast for the last ten days of the first month of winter to honor the hundred spirits, with la at the ancestral temple and sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 其方不熟，則闕其方之蠟焉。

translations.literal: If a direction's harvest was not ripe, that direction's la was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: If a direction's harvest was not ripe, that direction's la feast was omitted.

sentences.zh: 又以仲冬祭名源川澤於北郊，用一太牢。

translations.literal: Also in the second month of winter sacrificed to famous springs, rivers, and marshes at the northern suburb, using one great offering.
translations.idiomatic: Also in the second month of winter, famous springs, rivers, and marshes were sacrificed to at the northern suburb with a single great offering.

sentences.zh: 祭井于社宮，用一少牢。

translations.literal: Sacrificed to wells at the soil-altar palace, using one secondary offering.
translations.idiomatic: Wells were sacrificed to at the soil-altar palace with a single secondary offering.

sentences.zh: 季冬藏冰，仲春開冰，並用黑牡秬黍，於冰室祭司寒神。

translations.literal: At the last month of winter ice was stored; at the second month of spring ice was opened—both using black bull and black millet, at the ice chamber sacrificing to the Cold Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the last month of winter ice was stored; in the second month of spring it was opened—both rites used a black bull and black millet, sacrificing to the Cold Spirit at the ice chamber.

sentences.zh: 開冰，加以桃弧棘矢。

translations.literal: When opening ice, peach bow and thorn arrow were added.
translations.idiomatic: When the ice was opened, a peach-wood bow and thorn-wood arrow were added to the offering.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年十一月，詔曰：「古稱臘者，接也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Kaihuang, an edict said: 'Anciently la was called jie—taking the new and old in transition.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Kaihuang, an edict proclaimed: 'In antiquity la was called jie—marking the transition between old and new.'

sentences.zh: 取新故交接。

translations.literal: Taking the new and old in transition.
translations.idiomatic: It marked the handoff from old to new.

sentences.zh: 前周歲首，今之仲冬，建冬之月，稱蠟可也。

translations.literal: The former Zhou year's beginning is today's mid-winter; the month establishing winter—calling it la is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The former Zhou new year began at what is now mid-winter; the month that establishes winter may properly be called la.

sentences.zh: 後周用夏後之時，行姬氏之蠟。

translations.literal: Later Zhou used Xia's season but performed Ji Zhou's la.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou kept Xia's calendrical season but performed the Ji clan's la rite.

sentences.zh: 考諸先代，於義有違。

translations.literal: Examining previous generations, in meaning this was contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Examined against earlier practice, this was ritually inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 其十月行蠟者停，可以十二月為臘。

translations.literal: The la performed in the tenth month should cease; the twelfth month may serve as la.
translations.idiomatic: The la performed in the tenth month should be discontinued; the twelfth month should serve as la instead.

sentences.zh: 」於是始革前制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the previous system was first reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the old system was reformed for the first time.

sentences.zh: 後齊，正月晦日，中書舍人奏祓除。

translations.literal: Later Qi, on the last day of the first month, the Palace Scribe submitted the exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, on the last day of the first month the Palace Scribe performed the exorcism rite.

sentences.zh: 年暮上臺，東宮奏擇吉日詣殿堂，貴臣與師行事所須，皆移尚書省備設雲。

translations.literal: At year's end on the upper platform, the Eastern Palace submitted choosing an auspicious day to proceed to the hall; noble ministers and teachers' required items were all transferred to the Masters of Writing for preparation.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end on the upper platform, the Eastern Palace submitted the choice of an auspicious day to proceed to the hall; all items required by noble ministers and tutors were transferred to the Masters of Writing for preparation.

sentences.zh: 後主末年，祭非其鬼，至於躬自鼓儛，以事胡天。

translations.literal: In the last years of the Later Ruler, he sacrificed to spirits that were not his own—to the point of personally beating drums and dancing to serve the Hu Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of the Later Ruler, he sacrificed to spirits not his own—even personally beating drums and dancing in worship of the Hu Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鄴中遂多淫祀，茲風至今不絕。

translations.literal: In Ye thereupon arose many licentious shrines; this practice continues to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Ye thereupon filled with illicit shrines—a practice that continues to the present.

sentences.zh: 後周欲招來西域，又有拜胡天制，皇帝親焉。

translations.literal: Later Zhou, wishing to attract the Western Regions, also established a rite of bowing to the Hu Heaven, which the emperor personally performed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou, seeking to draw the Western Regions closer, also established a rite of bowing to the Hu Heaven, which the emperor performed in person.

sentences.zh: 其儀並從夷俗，淫僻不可紀也。

translations.literal: The ceremonies all followed barbarian custom—licentious and irregular beyond recording.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonies all followed foreign custom—licentious and irregular beyond proper record.
